universities.name: \. Jonkoping University
universities.desc: Jönköping University’s School of Engineering provides a three-year bachelor’s program in Mechanical Engineering and the program is taught in English. The program combines engineering fundamentals with practical learning and prepares students for further education or suitable technical careers. ![][image1]

universities.name: \. Uppsala universitet
universities.desc: Uppsala University provides education in engineering and related technical lines of study. The students are recommended to check the current bachelor catalog for mechanical engineering options and check the Swedish language requirements for each program. ![][image2]

universities.name: \. Royal Institute of Technology KTH
universities.location: \. Royal Institute of Technology KTH, Sweden
universities.desc: KTH is a large technical university in Stockholm with a large number of engineering and technology programs. Many bachelor’s programs in engineering require Swedish language proficiency, so international students should check the current bachelor’s listings and teaching languages. ![][image3] For the latest information on program availability, admission requirements and application deadlines, please visit University Admissions in Sweden. Please be aware that not all the universities on the list offer a bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering in English.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Mechanical Engineering (UG) in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Mechanical Engineering (UG) in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Mechanical Engineering (UG) in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
